name: Position-consistent joint K/V ToMe matching engineering gate
status: engineering only; no efficacy inference authorized
question: Can the existing position-consistent fixed-budget ToMe path use both native projected keys and values for matching, without changing its memory budget, temporal schedule, SAM2 weights, or native pre-compression behavior?
rationale: Memory-attention keys determine where a query reads, while values carry the retrieved content. Key-only matching can therefore pair tokens with similar attention affinity but different segmentation content. Concatenating separately normalized K and V descriptors gives each role equal metric weight. This is a mechanistic hypothesis, not a literature-established Dice improvement.

scope.targets: All post-prompt frames; the clip must exercise compression after more than six non-conditioning history maps.
scope.evidence_class: Real-clip engineering gate only. No efficacy or Dice claim.
scope.cohort_status: Previously analyzed development data; not an untouched confirmation set.

frozen_conditions.control: Position-consistent ToMe using only each layer's head-averaged, unrotated native projected-key metric.
frozen_conditions.candidate: Same position-consistent ToMe, but form the similarity metric by concatenating separately L2-normalized, head-averaged native K and V descriptors. The pinned ToMe matcher normalizes the concatenated metric before matching.
frozen_conditions.position: Both conditions use the ToMe destination token's representative spatial coordinate for SAM2 RoPE and copy its position embedding.
frozen_conditions.matching_and_aggregation: Reuse the pinned official ToMe bipartite soft matcher and mass-weighted means. All merges remain within frame and local 4x4 windows.
frozen_conditions.history: Same conditioning frame and same selected prior frame IDs, up to ten non-conditioning maps; no quality-based frame selection or confidence gates.
frozen_conditions.budget: Keep the dense 4096-token conditioning map and exactly 24576 non-conditioning spatial tokens after saturation; preserve the same per-frame and per-window quotas in both conditions.
frozen_conditions.sam2: Freeze all pretrained weights and retain native image features, memory writes, queries, decoder, object score, pointer behavior, and SAM2 temporal embeddings. Reuse the oldest native age slot for ages 7-10, then restore native state.

required_checks: Use the archived native checkpoint, configuration, manifest, prompt, runtime and frame inputs.
Before compression begins, match the archived native prediction and stored-state hashes exactly.
Exercise all four native SAM2 memory-attention layers on every target and verify the same 10-map quota plan in both conditions.
Verify finite K/V descriptors and outputs, source-token mass conservation, unchanged pointer inputs, correct K/V-position alignment, and unchanged SAM2 parameters.
Verify extended temporal-position state is restored after each run.
Run two fresh-process replays per condition and require matching frame, output, attention trace, quota and cluster-provenance hashes.
Confirm the K-only control and K/V candidate use identical per-frame and per-window token budgets.
stop_rule: Any parity, integrity, budget or replay failure blocks efficacy work. Fix only a demonstrated implementation error and repeat this gate. Passing this gate authorizes a separately frozen efficacy design; it does not show that Dice improves.

references.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
references.supports: Reusing bipartite similarity-based token matching and mass-weighted merging; not joint K/V matching for SAM2 or a Dice improvement.

references.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
references.supports: The frozen memory-attention architecture whose K/V projections and positional handling this gate exercises.

amendment: This gate adds a controlled matching-metric candidate after the existing position-consistent candidate passed its engineering gate. It changes the similarity descriptor only; no efficacy claim is authorized.
